title: First Bad Version
description:
You are a product manager currently leading a team to develop a new product. Unfortunately, the latest version of your product fails the quality check. Since each version is developed based on the previous version, all the versions after a bad version are also bad.

Suppose you have `n` versions `[1, 2, ..., n]` and you want to find out the first bad one, which causes all the following ones to be bad.

You are given an API `bool isBadVersion(version)` which returns whether `version` is bad. Implement a function `firstBadVersion(n)` to find the first bad version. You should minimize the number of calls to the API. Internally, `bad` is used by the judge to answer `isBadVersion(version)` and is not passed to your function.
hints: Because every version from the first bad version onward is bad, isBadVersion(v) is monotonic: false, ..., false, true, ..., true.
Use binary search on [1, n]: if isBadVersion(mid) is true, the first bad version is at mid or earlier (right = mid); otherwise it must be strictly after mid (left = mid + 1).
Compute mid as left + (right - left) / 2 to avoid 32-bit signed integer overflow when n is near 2^31 - 1.

examples.explanation: isBadVersion(3) is false and isBadVersion(4) is true, so version 4 is the first bad version.
There is only 1 version and it is bad, so return 1.
Version 1 is already bad, so all versions 1..10 are bad and the first bad version is 1.

inputs.name: n
inputs.description: Total number of versions (1 to n)
